item.title: The Complete Beginner's Guide to Solving Kakuro
item.description: Your first Kakuro grid looks like a crossword someone forgot to finish. Black squares are slashed with diagonal lines, small numbers sit in their corners, and rows of empty white boxes wait for you. You pick the first clue you see, a 15 across three cells, and start trying combinations. 9, 5, 1? 8, 4, 3? 7, 6, 2? Ten minutes later your eraser has worn a shiny patch into the paper and you haven’t committed a single digit.

item.title: How to Cross-Reference Intersecting Kakuro Clues
item.description:
You found the 3 in the corner of your Kakuro grid. Two cells, so it’s a 1 and a 2. You penciled both digits into both cells and felt good about it. Now you’re staring at those two cells, pencil hovering, and the question is simple: which one gets the 1?

You could flip a coin. Half the time you’d be right, and the other half you’d find out fifteen moves later, when a sum on the far side of the grid comes up one short. Knowing which digits belong in an entry is only half the work. The other half is knowing where each one goes, and the answer is almost never in the clue you’re staring at. It’s in the clue that crosses it.

item.title: Eliminating Guesswork in Kakuro: Parity and Logic
item.description:
You’re down to the last four squares of an expert Kakuro. You try one fill and every clue checks out. You erase it, try the other, and every clue checks out again. Your pencil hovers. One of them has to be wrong, and the puzzle has stopped giving you hints.

So you pick one. If you’re lucky, the grid finishes and you feel nothing. If you’re not, you find out eleven moves later, and now you can’t tell which of those eleven moves to undo.
